# Coder — Progress Memory

> **This file is the agent's persistent memory.** The `Coder` agent
> (`.github/agents/coder.agent.md`) MUST read this at session start and update it at session
> end. Keep it accurate and current. Commit it together with the work it describes.

## Mission

Implement the plans produced by the Planner agent for the `llm` VS Code extension. The Coder
is the **ONLY agent that writes code**. It keeps the build green at every step and commits
after each compiling step.

- [x] 1.100-16.S2-fix2 — `src/mcpManager.ts` only: Tester-found second defect in S2 (commits `dbad249` + fix `237e68c`) — when the `McpClient` constructor throws **synchronously** (input resolution happens before any `await`), the IIFE's catch block runs before `this.starting.set(name, p)`, so its `this.starting.delete(name)` is a no-op and the already-rejected promise `p` is then stored in `starting` and never removed. Consequence: after a `missing required input` failure the server is permanently stuck — every subsequent `ensureStarted(name)` (even after `setInputs`) hits the in-flight check and returns the cached stale rejection. Fix: added `p.catch(() => this.starting.delete(name));` immediately after `this.starting.set(name, p);` — the microtask runs after the set, so the delete actually removes the entry; idempotent with the existing in-catch/finally deletes on the async failure path (calling delete twice is harmless). No IIFE restructure, no catch-block change. Async failure path (handshake failure) was already correct (its catch runs after the set). Compile clean.
- [x] 1.100-16.S2-fix — `src/mcp.ts` only: Tester-found defect in S2 commit `dbad249` — the `McpClient` constructor gated `resolveMcpInputs` behind `inputs && Object.keys(inputs).length > 0`, so when `McpManager.ensureStarted` passed `undefined` (no `setInputs` ever called), a server whose `env` contains `${input:API_KEY}` spawned with the literal `${input:API_KEY}` string instead of failing with `missing required input: API_KEY`. Fix: removed the gate; the constructor now always computes `const env = resolveMcpInputs(config, inputs ?? {})` and spawns with `env: { ...process.env, ...env }`. `resolveMcpInputs` already handles the no-refs case (returns the env map unchanged; `{}` when `cfg.env` undefined), so behavior with no `${input:...}` refs is byte-identical to before. `src/mcpManager.ts` catch block untouched (already surfaces the throw via `error` status + `notify`). Compile clean.

## Notes / decisions

- The Coder is the ONLY agent that writes code.
- One step per session. Each step independently compiles and commits.
- No runtime npm dependencies. No bundler. Stay minimal.
- Always update this file in the same commit as the code it describes.
